assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology and incretin-based therapy form one of the most consequential translational arcs in modern medicine: a gut hormone mechanism became a treatment class that lowers glycemia, body weight and cardiovascular events. The discovery is original, clear and has transformed diabetes and obesity care.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology and secretion of GLP-1 and its incretin role), Drucker (GLP-1 biology, receptor actions, translation) and Knudsen (design of long-acting acylated analogues leading to liraglutide and semaglutide) cover mechanism through therapy. Mojsov's sequence and activity contribution is credited in the candidate but cannot fit within three; as I recall, other early contributors such as Habener are not on this list. Allocation is contested.
assessment.maturity: Clinical efficacy is confirmed by large independent outcome trials and wide global use for over a decade, and the mechanistic basis is stable. Recognition is timely, arguably pressing.
uncertainties: Priority disputes around early GLP-1 peptide characterization and the three-person limit
Whether the prize should reward physiology, drug design, or both
Long-term safety and durability of obesity effects are still accruing (my recollection, not verified)

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineering a patient's T cells to recognize and kill cancer created a new therapeutic modality with durable remissions in refractory B-cell leukemias and lymphomas and now expanding into myeloma and autoimmune disease. Original concept, clear proof of efficacy, large impact.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (early CAR design with costimulation and clinical translation), June (clinical development of CD19 CAR-T with durable responses) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell therapy and early gene-engineered TIL/TCR work) represent decisive contributions. Eshhar, Kuwana and others who made first-generation chimeric receptors are not on the credited list, so the credit set is incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and a decade of long-term follow-up confirm efficacy in hematologic cancer; solid tumors remain unresolved. Timing is reasonable but toxicity and access issues persist.
uncertainties: Missing early inventors (not on the supplied credit list) complicate fair attribution
Limited efficacy in solid tumors
Long-term safety including secondary malignancy is still being characterized

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle vaccines against HPV are a clear, original discovery with direct cancer prevention: strong population-level reductions in HPV infection, cervical precancer and cervical cancer. The link to the earlier Nobel-recognized HPV-cancer discovery makes the story coherent.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller (L1 VLP self-assembly and immunogenicity, NCI) and Frazer (L1/L2 VLP work with Zhou, who is deceased and not on the list) form a plausible trio. Priority among groups (Georgetown, Rochester, Queensland, NCI) was contested and settled partly by patents. I cannot verify the details independently.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature: licensed vaccines for nearly two decades with real-world evidence of cancer reduction in vaccinated cohorts and independent confirmation.
uncertainties: Historical priority disputes among VLP groups
Exclusion of deceased contributor Jian Zhou
Whether the field is considered already recognized via prior HPV-cancer prize

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Showing that TNF is a dominant driver in rheumatoid arthritis and that blocking it produces clinical benefit created the biologic era for inflammatory disease, extended to IBD, psoriasis and spondyloarthritis. Concept, proof in patients and impact on disease course are all clear.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini jointly formulated the TNF hypothesis in synovial cultures and led the first trials of infliximab; the pairing is clean and widely accepted. Contributions from Cerami, Vilcek, Kollias and others on TNF biology or antibody development could be argued but the translational discovery is well captured by two names.
assessment.maturity: Over twenty-five years of clinical use with independent confirmation; the interpretation is stable. Slightly less novel now that several other cytokine blockades exist, but timing is not premature.
uncertainties: Credit for TNF biology and antibody engineering is distributed beyond the two names
Possible perception of field crowding in immune-mediated disease

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rational targeting of the BCR-ABL kinase with imatinib turned chronic myeloid leukemia from a fatal disease into a manageable one, and established the paradigm of kinase-directed targeted cancer therapy. Very high clarity and impact.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (compound program at Ciba-Geigy), Druker (preclinical proof and clinical leadership) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors) are the standard trio. Contributions from Rowley, Witte, Baltimore and others on the underlying biology were separately honored or are not listed; Zimmermann's chemistry may be overlooked.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature with decades of survival data and many follow-on kinase inhibitors; recognition is long-awaited rather than premature.
uncertainties: Chemistry credit (Zimmermann) not on supplied list
Part of the underlying biology of BCR-ABL arises from earlier work outside this candidate

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics provided genetically targeted, millisecond control of defined cell populations, becoming a core method of neuroscience with growing therapeutic application in vision restoration. Original, widely transformative as a tool, though the prize category favors discovery with medical relevance.
assessment.attribution: Nagel, Bamberg and Hegemann discovered and characterized channelrhodopsin; Deisseroth and Boyden demonstrated neuronal control and developed the toolkit; Miesenböck made an earlier, distinct genetically encoded photoactivation demonstration. Six credited names cannot fit within three, so any trio leaves out strong claims.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with broad independent replication over twenty years; clinical translation is early.
uncertainties: Severe attribution contest and six-name credit set
Whether a research tool is judged sufficiently medicine-related
Clinical impact still emerging

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense modulation of SMN2 splicing yielded nusinersen, the first effective disease-modifying therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, with dramatic survival and motor benefits in infants. A clear mechanism-to-therapy story that validated splice-switching oligonucleotides.
assessment.attribution: Krainer (splicing mechanism and ISS-N1 target identification) and Bennett (antisense chemistry and drug development at Ibis/Isis) are well matched. Others such as Singh and Hua contributed experimental work, and the SMA gene discovery by Melki and Lefebvre is a separate upstream contribution.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with strong clinical confirmation and years of follow-up; the broader antisense platform further supports the interpretation. Timing is reasonable.
uncertainties: Attribution of the SMN gene discovery versus therapy
Competing SMA treatments (gene therapy, small molecules) may affect framing

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cGAS-STING pathway defined how cytosolic DNA is sensed to trigger interferon and inflammatory responses, with links to antiviral defense, autoinflammation, cancer immunity and senescence. A fundamental and original mechanism with wide implications.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and the cGAMP second messenger; Barber and Ishikawa discovered STING. Sun and Wu were on the cGAS work as co-authors, and the cGAMP structure involved other groups, so five names exceed the three-laureate limit. Chen plus the STING discoverers cover the key steps, but allocation is open.
assessment.maturity: Discovered roughly 2008 to 2013 with extensive independent confirmation; therapeutic translation (STING agonists, inhibitors) is not yet validated, so the discovery is more established than its clinical consequences.
uncertainties: Therapeutic impact not yet demonstrated
Allocation among five credited names
Possible argument that recognition may be somewhat early
